title: Hosted API: customer proposals reconciliation and eligibility decisioning
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We receive a high volume of customer feature proposals that span chat streaming, function/tool calling, and structured outputs. The current ad-hoc triage creates long handoffs, inconsistent routing to Dedicated/Private offerings, and missed enterprise readiness signals (SLA, egress/compliance, KMS). Goal: Define a reconciliatory intake + eligibility decisioning flow that automatically classifies requests, surfaces cost/latency risk, and routes to the correct engagement path (self-serve backlog, engineering intake, Solutions/SE, or enterprise sales). The flow should reduce manual triage time, standardize required artifacts, and enable SLO/SLA gating for routing decisions.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic decision matrix exists that classifies incoming hosted API feature proposals into at least: Self-Serve, Quick-Config, Engineering Work, Solutions Assisted, Enterprise (Dedicated/Private)
Automated ingestion extracts signals: request type (chat/streaming/tool-call/structured), estimated RPS and token cost, data-sensitivity flags, requested SLAs, and compliance constraints
Dashboard shows volume and disposition within 24 hours of intake for 95% of proposals
Routing rules integrated with intake form trigger required artifact workflows (security checklist, sample prompt set, evaluation rubric) before Engineering intake
Metrics/telemetry events defined for each stage for future ML-assisted triage improvements
notes: Design constraints: keep developer friction low for self-serve while capturing enterprise signals early
We must avoid blocking low-risk streaming feature requests that only need minor SDK tweaks
Integrate with existing Salesforce contact record and Support ticket tags so Solutions/SE are notified for high-revenue customers
Consider using a scoring model (0-100) combining cost risk, latency sensitivity, data sensitivity, and revenue potential; threshold mapping documented in matrix
proposed_decision_matrix: Score inputs: estimated peak RPS, avg tokens per request, streaming required (boolean), function/tool orchestration complexity (0-3), structured-output strictness (schema required), customer SLA level, data sensitivity

Routing thresholds: 0-20 -> Self-Serve, 21-40 -> Quick-Config (Console guidance + templates), 41-70 -> Engineering Work (backlog), 71-85 -> Solutions Assisted, 86-100 -> Enterprise Dedicated/Private intake
Example: A fintech customer requesting streaming with function-chaining and PCI-adjacent data => high data-sensitivity + SLA => likely 90+ -> Enterprise path
telemetry_and_dashboards: Events: intake_submitted, auto_classified_score, routed_to_queue, docs_requested, security_check_complete, engineering_triage_started, resolution_disposition
Dashboard KPIs: time_to_route_median, percent_auto_routed, percent_requires_manual_review, avg_time_in_engineering_queue, disposition_by_request_type
Initial Grafana dashboard prototype: dashboards/hosted-intake/triage-overview (linked in attachments)
required_artifacts_before_engineering: Minimal reproducible prompt set (5 representative calls) with expected outputs
Requested schema (if structured output) or example toolchain spec
Customer SLA and compliance notes (KMS, retention policy, region requests)
routing_examples: Low-cost embedding/one-off chat customization with no SLA -> Self-Serve + docs template
Streaming chat for high-concurrency analytics with <100ms P95 requirement -> Quick-Config if within hosted capacity else Engineering Work
Function-calling orchestration that spawns backend side-effects and needs idempotency guarantees -> Engineering Work + Security checklist
Enterprise onboarding requesting VPC + HSM -> Enterprise Dedicated/Private and Solutions sales handoff
open_questions: Should we expose the auto-classification score to customers to explain routing? (UX trade-off)
How aggressive should automatic fallback routing be when signals are incomplete? (delay vs. ask for more info)
Do we need a separate SLA gating for streaming vs. non-streaming workloads?
Operational cost: who will maintain the scoring model and thresholds? (PM + Data Eng + Solutions)
Localization: should region-based capacity constraints alter routing thresholds?
